㊥ (implementing the two speed-ups) I've sent both out. zai-2 will measure how long a warm run takes on the blank path, both unchanged and after a compiler edit, and what invalidates the cache. codex-6 will build a probe that compiles one named declaration on its own, through the same rebuild path the blank run uses. That way, a check like "does `testParseModule` compile now?" should take seconds or minutes instead of 11 minutes. Both are parked together as `park-de7d7ce9`, with the session field and a 60-minute backstop.

㊢ (jobs and ids)
- zai-2, warm timings: `invoke-…a1899792` → `WARM.md`
- codex-6, probe tool: `invoke-…00e89fc5` → `PROBE.md`. Test and tool as separate commits. Its real check is to reproduce the `term#[_,]` stop and time it against the 11-minute cold run.
- codex-4, curriculum, still running: `invoke-…ddaddf17` → `BLANK-CURRICULUM.tsv`

🈲 (keeping the jobs apart) zai-2 and codex-6 each work in their own worktree, with a copy of the warm generated cache. codex-4 is reading the cache in `/tmp/mfs-blank` for its curriculum job, so the other two must not write there. All three briefs repeat the rule about never deleting under `data/tmp/lean`.

㊭ (how it fits together) When all three report, each fix should follow this loop:
1. Pick the next failing row in the curriculum.
2. Fix it.
3. Probe that declaration to confirm the fix.
4. Run warm to check that nothing else regressed.

The cold 11-minute run then serves only as acceptance for a batch of fixes. Progress shows up as the curriculum's "compiled" count going up.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (the loop) The fix is in `/tmp/mfs-blank`: `5e44804` adds the test and `da42b39` makes the change. Each lookup may now rebuild a given declaration only once. If a declaration is still missing after its own rebuild, the run fails with an error naming it. The retry still moves forward through *different* declarations, and since there are finitely many, it can't run forever. The new test hung on codex-4's version (I killed it at 30 s) and passes now. All 3 blank-startup tests pass. It isn't on startup-linux yet; I'll land it there along with codex-4's two commits.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text: (what the existing curriculum covered) PLAN.md does have a curriculum, but it doesn't cover what you need now. Its Phase 1 and 2 maps compare *which syntax kinds exist* in Lean and in the port. Blank startup instead depends on *which code runs*, and nothing in the plan lists that. So each run has only shown us the next stop. The census has part of the answer: just 26 constants are recorded as executed after init for an empty file (`ParserFn.run`, `mkParserState`, `FileMap.ofString`, `Trie.find?`, extension `mkInitial`s and so on). That table only covers the 20,173 initializer-closure rows, though. It leaves out the parse loop itself, including `testParseModule`, where we're stopped now.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(what the new job produces) `BLANK-CURRICULUM.tsv` and `.md`:
1. Every constant Lean executes after init for `empty.lean`, from a fresh callgrind run, each with file:line.
2. A check that the port's entry point, `testParseModule`, does the same parse as `lean empty.lean`'s frontend, with any differences named.
3. For each constant, the macros and notations in its body that the port must expand to compile it (`term#[_,]` is one).
4. The port's status for each: compiled, failed with an error, or not reached, taken from evidence only.
5. Counts.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-4
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the fork-Python idea) I'd put it after the curriculum. Forking at minute 10 only helps when a fix lands in code the parent process hasn't loaded yet. Our fixes are almost all in the compiler, which is already loaded and holding state by then. Two cheaper ways to shorten each attempt:
- Run warm. S2 brought an unchanged warm start down to 41 s, so cold runs can be kept for acceptance.
- Use the curriculum's per-declaration probes.

previous_reply_acts.text: (bell issue, for the agent you pass it to) The spec in short: a park on an `emacs*` surface with no `session` is queued under `[agent ""]`, which the buffer never polls (`agent-repl-park.el:307`). Meanwhile `auto-bellback-suppressing-park` (`http.clj` ~1290) drops the bellback because "a park will wake the agent". The result is that the wake is lost with no signal. There are 17 stuck items for claude-4 in `/tmp/futon3c-parked-on.edn`. Fix either by rejecting such parks at POST, or by suppressing the bellback only after the ready item has been leased and acked. Then clear the stale queue.
